## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type
- Verdict: confirmed
- Confidence: high
- Severity: medium
- Task type: correctness and regression-test fix

### Root Cause
The GitHub projector already has the required read-modify-replace behavior, but workflow-state derivation is split between a partial local helper in `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` and isolated parent terminal handling. Bounded checkpoint transitions therefore update only some labels, and the parent-owned merge lifecycle never projects `workflow:awaiting-merge` before merge or `workflow:merged` at merge completion.

### Evidence
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts` defines the canonical workflow label values but does not provide one shared checkpoint mapping.
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts:1102-1132` maps only selected child starts and investigation completion; it has no merge mapping and relies on text matching for invalid investigation results.
- The checkpoint handler invokes the local mapping only for child checkpoint calls, while parent merge transitions use `appendPhase` in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` and do not call `setWorkflowLabel` at merge start/completion.
- `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel` filters all existing `workflow:*` labels and retains unrelated labels, so the projection primitive satisfies the replacement/preservation requirement and should be reused unchanged.
- Existing tests verify isolated label replacement and one exact label assertion, but do not exercise the complete checkpoint lifecycle or parent merge projections.

### Affected Files
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts` — add the shared action/phase-to-canonical-label mapping.
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` — replace the duplicate partial mapping with the shared helper.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — project awaiting-merge when parent merge starts and merged after the merge effect succeeds.
- `test/core/artifact-protocol.test.ts` — cover every child lifecycle mapping and invalid-investigation branch.
- `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts` — retain/extend replacement and unrelated-label preservation coverage if needed.

### Recommendation
Centralize checkpoint label derivation beside `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE`, preserve the current invalid-investigation classification, use the shared helper from bounded checkpoint handling, and explicitly call the existing projector at parent merge start and completion. Keep all label writes fail-closed and leave the projector's unrelated-label preservation semantics unchanged.

### Related Issues
- No duplicate implementation or open duplicate issue was found in the supplied issue context or read-only repository state.

### Decomposition Assessment
The change is coherent and bounded to label derivation, parent merge projection, and focused tests. No product, UX, protected-branch, or security-authority decision is required.

### Acceptance Spec
- Every child phase start receives the canonical current workflow label.
- Investigation completion selects ready-to-build or invalid from the existing report classification.
- Parent merge start projects workflow:awaiting-merge; successful merge completion projects workflow:merged.
- Each projection removes stale workflow:* labels while preserving unrelated labels.
- Automated tests cover the full mapping and replacement behavior without adding external side effects.

## Builder Contract

### Objective
Ensure every ForgeDock workflow transition projects the canonical current workflow:* label, removing stale workflow labels while preserving unrelated labels.

### Allowed Paths
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts`
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts`
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`
- `test/core/artifact-protocol.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes
- Do not change GitHub authentication, lease, state-journal, review, merge authorization, close authority, cleanup authority, or protected-branch policy.
- Do not rewrite `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel` semantics or add direct GitHub mutation paths.
- Do not mark `workflow:merged` before the merge effect succeeds.
- Do not remove unrelated issue labels or change non-workflow labels.
- Do not add credentials, production data, issue-body content, generated artifacts, or unapproved verification commands.

### Invariants
1. Canonical workflow label values remain defined by `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE`.
2. One shared phase/action mapping is the only source for child checkpoint label derivation and parent merge labels.
3. Investigation completion preserves the existing invalid-versus-ready classification.
4. Child starts map investigate to investigating, plan/prepare-worktree/implement/verify to building, and review to in-review.
5. Parent merge start maps to awaiting-merge; merged is projected only after the successful merge effect and merge checkpoint.
6. Every label write uses the existing projector, which removes all workflow:* labels and preserves unrelated labels.
7. Empty local verification policy remains valid; no command is invented.

### Deliverables
- Shared typed checkpoint-to-workflow-label helper beside canonical label constants.
- Child runtime wired to the shared helper with no duplicate mapping.
- Parent merge start/completion label projections bound to successful phase ordering.
- Regression tests covering the lifecycle mapping and workflow-label replacement/preservation.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### History
- Issue #92 is a confirmed regression in the frozen staging base; prior cancelled attempts do not alter the current source contract.
- The current projector already implements safe workflow-label replacement, so the defect is derivation/timing rather than label-set mutation.

### Callers and Data Flow
- `forge_checkpoint` in `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` persists the typed event, projects the checkpoint artifact, derives a workflow label, and calls `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel`.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` owns merge/close/cleanup after the child returns ready-for-merge; it must project awaiting-merge after merge starts and merged only after `mergePullRequest` plus the merge completion checkpoint.
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts` is the canonical protocol module and is imported by both child and parent code after this change.
- Existing adapter tests provide a deterministic transport with a `bug` label and assert stale workflow labels are removed.

### CI Surface
- The trusted run policy has an empty `verification.commands` map, so no `forge_verify` check is available; GitHub CI is parent-owned.
- Use focused source reads, LSP diagnostics, `forge_diff`, and the committed regression tests as evidence without inventing a named Forge verification command.

### Prior Findings
- Existing child mapping at `src/agents/child-runtime.ts:1102-1132` is partial and duplicated.
- Parent merge transitions in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` do not project awaiting-merge or merged at the relevant boundaries.
- Existing tests cover isolated replacement and one exact label, not the full lifecycle mapping.

### Hazards
- Projecting merged before a successful merge would misrepresent durable state.
- Mapping review completion or merge start incorrectly could leave a stale in-review label or claim merge authority prematurely.
- Changing the projector could regress preservation of `bug` and other unrelated labels.
- Duplicate mapping logic could drift again between child and parent paths.

## Implementation Plan

1. Add a typed shared `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` helper to `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts`, using canonical constants and preserving invalid-investigation report handling. Check IDs: `canonical-mapping`, `invalid-classification`.
2. Replace the local child-runtime mapping with the shared helper and keep checkpoint projection ordering unchanged. Check IDs: `child-reuse`, `child-lifecycle`.
3. Import the helper in `src/workflows/work-on.ts`; project awaiting-merge after parent merge start and workflow:merged only after the successful merge effect/complete checkpoint. Check IDs: `merge-awaiting`, `merge-merged`, `merge-ordering`.
4. Extend protocol tests for all child phase starts, investigation completion branches, and parent merge actions. Extend projector coverage for stale workflow replacement and unrelated-label preservation across repeated transitions. Check IDs: `mapping-tests`, `replacement-preservation`.
5. Run primary diagnostics, inspect the final diff against the frozen base, create the implementation commit, prepare the bound PR, and execute the required fresh review panel. Check IDs: `diagnostics`, `diff-identity`, `review-gates`.

### Acceptance Mapping
- `canonical-mapping`, `invalid-classification` → canonical shared mapping and preserved investigation classification.
- `child-reuse`, `child-lifecycle` → bounded checkpoint lifecycle uses one helper.
- `merge-awaiting`, `merge-merged`, `merge-ordering` → parent transitions project labels at durable merge boundaries.
- `mapping-tests`, `replacement-preservation` → complete mapping and safe label replacement regression coverage.
- `diagnostics`, `diff-identity`, `review-gates` → implementation readiness and required review authority.

### Out of Scope
- Issue/PR content or label API redesign.
- Changes to workflow state-machine legality, review gates, merge policy, close, cleanup, or orchestration.
- New local verification commands, GitHub CI changes, or runtime sandboxing.
- Automatic reconciliation of historical labels outside the current transition path.
